verdict.summary:
DRAFT FOR REVIEW BY A QUALIFIED FINANCE/ACCOUNTING PROFESSIONAL. Not regulatory, tax or investment advice.

SUBJECT: Level 2A and Level 2B liquid asset amounts under 12 CFR 329.21(b)(2)-(3), and their sum.
PERIOD: As of the calculation date (single date; no averaging, no transition provisions applied).
CURRENCY: US dollars (USD), stated in whole dollars; fair value inputs given in millions.
BASIS: Fair value of eligible HQLA, unadjusted liquid asset amounts per 329.21(b) (NOT the unwind-adjusted amounts per 329.21(f)). Institution type: FDIC-supervised institution.

=====================================================================
1. SOURCE TEXT RELIED ON (verbatim, as reproduced on the cited pages)
=====================================================================
12 CFR 329.21(b)(2): "The level 2A liquid asset amount equals 85 percent of the fair value of all level 2A liquid assets held by the FDIC-supervised institution as of the calculation date that are eligible HQLA."

12 CFR 329.21(b)(3): "The level 2B liquid asset amount equals 50 percent of the fair value of all level 2B liquid assets held by the FDIC-supervised institution as of the calculation date that are eligible HQLA."

Sources (all four reproductions agree on the 85% and 50% factors):
- https://ecfr.gov/current/title-12/part-329/section-329.21 (fetched 2026-11-23T12:03:48Z, sha256 ca896132ac72)
- https://ecfr.gov/current/title-12/part-329 (fetched 2026-11-23T12:03:49Z, sha256 f177572c4517)
- https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2026-title12-vol5/xhtml/CFR-2026-title12-vol5-part329-subpartC.html (fetched 2026-11-23T12:03:48Z, sha256 cc1e1f23af77)
- https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2026-title12-vol5/pdf/CFR-2026-title12-vol5-part329.pdf (fetched 2026-11-23T12:03:48Z, sha256 7667c6fd7fe2)

Note: 329.21(f)(3) repeats the same 50 percent factor for the unwind-adjusted level 2B amount, so the factor is not in dispute between the unadjusted and adjusted computations; only the asset base differs, and per instruction no unwind is applied.

=====================================================================
2. INPUTS (all stated as given; none is derived by me)
=====================================================================
I-1  Fair value of level 2A liquid assets, all eligible HQLA   = $80,000,000
I-2  Fair value of level 2B liquid assets, all eligible HQLA   = $30,000,000
I-3  Level 2A factor per 329.21(b)(2)                          = 0.85  (i.e. a 15% haircut)
I-4  Level 2B factor per 329.21(b)(3)                          = 0.50  (i.e. a 50% haircut)
I-5  Level 1 liquid asset amount                               = NOT PROVIDED (see Section 6)
I-6  Reserve balance requirement under 12 CFR 204.5            = NOT APPLICABLE to 2A/2B (329.21(b)(1) deducts it from Level 1 only)

=====================================================================
3. COMPUTATION - LEVEL 2A LIQUID ASSET AMOUNT  [ASK 2]
=====================================================================
Rule: 329.21(b)(2) - 85 percent of fair value of eligible level 2A liquid assets.

  Level 2A liquid asset amount = 0.85 x $80,000,000
                               = $68,000,000

Arithmetic shown in millions: 80.0 x 0.85 = 68.0
Cross-check: haircut retained = 80.0 x 0.15 = 12.0; 80.0 - 12.0 = 68.0. Agrees.
Cross-check: 68.0 / 80.0 = 0.85, reproducing the regulatory factor exactly.

=====================================================================
4. COMPUTATION - LEVEL 2B LIQUID ASSET AMOUNT  [ASK 2]
=====================================================================
Rule: 329.21(b)(3) - 50 percent of fair value of eligible level 2B liquid assets.

  Level 2B liquid asset amount = 0.50 x $30,000,000
                               = $15,000,000

Arithmetic shown in millions: 30.0 x 0.50 = 15.0
Cross-check: haircut retained = 30.0 x 0.50 = 15.0; 30.0 - 15.0 = 15.0. Agrees.
Cross-check: 15.0 / 30.0 = 0.50, reproducing the regulatory factor exactly.

=====================================================================
5. SUM  [ASK 3]
=====================================================================
  Level 2A liquid asset amount           $68,000,000
+ Level 2B liquid asset amount           $15,000,000
= Sum of level 2A + level 2B amounts     $83,000,000

Arithmetic shown in millions: 68.0 + 15.0 = 83.0

Basis of the sum: arithmetic addition only. No netting, no deduction of any excess HQLA amount, no reserve-balance deduction (that applies to Level 1 only), and no combination with Level 1 (not provided).

=====================================================================
6. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT APPLIED (the "ignoring other caps and adjustments" instruction)
=====================================================================
The following provisions of 329.21 exist but are OUT OF SCOPE for this calculation by instruction. They are reproduced here only so the reviewer can see exactly what was excluded, not because they were computed.

(a) Level 2 cap excess amount, 329.21(d): greater of [level 2A amount + level 2B amount - 0.6667 x level 1 amount] and 0. With 68.0 + 15.0 = 83.0, this expression is 83.0 - 0.6667 x L1. Because 0.6667 is approximately 2/3, the cap binds unless L1 is at least about 1.5 x 83.0 = $124.5 million. L1 is NOT PROVIDED, so this excess amount cannot be computed and is not applied.

(b) Level 2B cap excess amount, 329.21(e): greater of [level 2B amount - level 2 cap excess amount - 0.1765 x (level 1 amount + level 2A amount)] and 0. Depends on L1 via the level 2 cap excess amount; not computable without L1. Not applied.

(c) Unadjusted / adjusted excess HQLA amount, 329.21(c) and (g)-(i), and the deduction of the greater of them in 329.21(a)(4). Not applied.

(d) Unwind adjustment of liquid asset amounts, 329.21(f)(1)-(3) (secured funding, secured lending, asset exchange, collateralized derivatives maturing within 30 calendar days). Not applied; the amounts in Sections 3 and 4 are the unadjusted amounts under 329.21(b), not the adjusted amounts under 329.21(f).

(e) Operational and eligibility requirements in 329.22 (monetization capability, etc.) are taken as satisfied by the instruction that all $80 million and $30 million are eligible HQLA.

IMPORTANT REVIEWER POINT: because of (a)-(d), the $83,000,000 in Section 5 is NOT the institution's HQLA amount under 329.21(a). The HQLA amount would be 68.0 + 15.0 + L1 - max(unadjusted excess, adjusted excess). With a binding level 2 cap and a small L1 balance, the entire $83.0 million could be deducted in arriving at the HQLA amount. The figures here answer only the two liquid-asset-amount questions posed.

=====================================================================
7. ASSUMPTIONS TABLE (each is an assumption, not a sourced fact)
=====================================================================
A-1  The cited reproduction of Part 329 is the operative text for FDIC-supervised institutions on the calculation date, not a superseded or proposed version. Basis: four independent fetches (eCFR section page, eCFR part page, govinfo XHTML, govinfo PDF, 2026 edition) all show 85% and 50% identically.
A-2  All $80 million of level 2A and all $30 million of level 2B assets are eligible HQLA and satisfy 329.22. Given by the request.
A-3  "Fair value" is the correct measurement basis as of the calculation date; no subsequent-event or settlement-date adjustment. Given by the request.
A-4  No reserve balance requirement offsets apply to level 2A or 2B. Follows from the text of 329.21(b)(1).
A-5  Amounts are USD. Follows from the FDIC/US supervisory context.
A-6  "Resulting amounts" means the post-haircut amounts under 329.21(b)(2)-(3), pre-cap. Basis: the express instruction to ignore other caps and adjustments.
A-7  No transitional or phase-in provision applies on the calculation date.
A-8  Figures are point-in-time, not averages over a 30-day or 90-day window.

=====================================================================
8. ANSWER SUMMARY
=====================================================================
Level 2A liquid asset amount  = $68,000,000  (0.85 x $80,000,000)
Level 2B liquid asset amount  = $15,000,000  (0.50 x $30,000,000)
Sum                           = $83,000,000  ($68,000,000 + $15,000,000)

All figures USD, as of the calculation date, fair value basis, unadjusted for unwind, before application of any cap or excess HQLA deduction.

=====================================================================
9. FALSIFIERS (what would change these numbers)
=====================================================================
F-1  If the operative text used factors other than 85% / 50%, both amounts change proportionally. Trigger: any of the four cited sources showing a different percentage.
F-2  If any of the $80 million / $30 million were found not to be eligible HQLA, the base falls and the amounts fall with it.
F-3  If "resulting amounts" were intended to mean post-cap amounts, then Level 1 holdings become a required input and neither $68,000,000 nor $15,000,000 is the answer; the level 2 cap excess amount under 329.21(d) would have to be computed and deducted.
F-4  If the institution were not FDIC-supervised (e.g. a different Part 329 applicability), the applicable subpart and any differing factor would need re-checking.

DRAFT FOR REVIEW BY A QUALIFIED FINANCE/ACCOUNTING PROFESSIONAL — NOT FINANCIAL, TAX OR INVESTMENT ADVICE.

SUBJECT: Minimum CET1 and tier 1 capital ratios, calendar year 2014 (Jan 1 – Dec 31, 2014), advanced approaches national bank that is not a savings and loan holding company (OCC jurisdiction, 12 CFR Part 3). Buffers and other add-ons excluded per instruction.
PERIOD: January 1, 2014 through December 31, 2014 (calendar-year 2014 transition period).
CURRENCY / BASIS: Capital ratios are dimensionless percentages (capital ÷ risk-weighted assets); the underlying capital and RWA amounts are in USD but no USD amounts are used here. Ratios are stated on the regulatory (transition) basis, not the bank's actual reported ratios, and are gross of buffers/add-ons.

1. ANSWER TABLE

| Ask | Measure | Minimum ratio | Source provision |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | CET1 capital ratio, 1/1/2014–12/31/2014 (advanced approaches national bank, not an SLHC) | 4.0% | 12 CFR 3.1(f)(1)(iii)(A) (eCFR); transition schedule originally adopted at 78 FR 62157, 62273 (Oct. 11, 2013) |
| 1 | Tier 1 capital ratio, 1/1/2014–12/31/2014 (same bank) | 5.5% | same provision |
| 2 | CET1 capital ratio stated in the text of 12 CFR Part 3 reproduced on the cited page (§ 3.10(a)) | 4.5% | 12 CFR 3.10(a)(1) [2014 CFR print] / 3.10(a)(1)(i) [eCFR] |
| 2 | Tier 1 capital ratio stated in the text of 12 CFR Part 3 reproduced on the cited page (§ 3.10(a)) | 6.0% | 12 CFR 3.10(a)(2) [2014 CFR print] / 3.10(a)(1)(ii) [eCFR] |

Comparison / arithmetic (percentage points, pp):
- CET1: 4.5% (rule-text minimum) − 4.0% (2014 transition minimum) = 0.5 pp step-up.
- Tier 1: 6.0% (rule-text minimum) − 5.5% (2014 transition minimum) = 0.5 pp step-up.
- No ratio in this memo exceeds, or is derived by exceeding, any threshold stated in the same memo; all four figures are direct quotations.

2. WHY THE TWO SETS OF NUMBERS DIFFER (and both are correct)

§ 3.10(a) states the steady-state minimums. The 2014 CFR print reads: '§ 3.10 Minimum capital requirements. (a) Minimum capital requirements. A national bank or Federal savings association must maintain the following minimum capital ratios: (1) A common equity tier 1 capital ratio of 4.5 percent. (2) A tier 1 capital ratio of 6 percent. (3) A total capital ratio of 8 percent. (4) A leverage ratio of 4 percent. (5) For advanced approaches national banks or Federal savings associations, a supplementary leverage ratio of 3 percent. (6) For Federal savings associations, a tangible capital ratio of 1.5 percent.' The current eCFR reproduces the same two figures at § 3.10(a)(1)(i)–(ii).

Those headline minimums are expressly subject to the transition provisions. § 3.1(f) ('Timing') provides that an advanced approaches national bank or Federal savings association that is not a savings and loan holding company must, '(iii) Beginning on January 1, 2014, calculate and maintain minimum capital ratios in accordance with subparts A, B, and C of this part, provided, however, that such national bank or Federal savings association must: (A) From January 1, 2014 to December 31, 2014, maintain a minimum common equity tier 1 capital ratio of 4 percent, a minimum tier 1 capital ratio of 5.5 percent, a minimum total capital ratio of 8 percent, and a minimum leverage ratio of 4 percent.'

Therefore: for the bank in scope, the operative 2014 minimums are 4.0% CET1 and 5.5% tier 1 (Ask 1). The 4.5% / 6.0% figures in § 3.10(a) are the minimums stated in the rule text (Ask 2); they become the operative minimums when the 2014 transition step-down ceases to apply (i.e., from January 1, 2015), subject to the buffer phase-in that begins January 1, 2016.

3. WHY THE ADVANCED APPROACHES STATUS MATTERS FOR 2014

The 2014 transition applies to advanced approaches banks only. § 3.1(f)(4): 'No national bank or Federal savings association that is not an advanced approaches bank or advanced approaches savings association is subject to this part 3 until January 1, 2015.' So the reason a ratio applied at all during 2014 is the bank's advanced approaches status. Similarly, the capital adjustment/deduction transition runs 'Beginning January 1, 2014 for an advanced approaches national bank ... through December 31, 2017' (§ 3.22(b) transition text quoted from the 2014 CFR print).

Note that the advanced approaches 'lower of standardized / advanced approaches' calculation method (§ 3.10(c) in the 2014 print; § 3.10(d) in the current eCFR) changes how the ratio is computed, not the minimum percentage it must meet. The 2014 transition percentages above are the minimums against which that computed ratio is measured.

4. TREATMENT OF BUFFERS AND OTHER ADD-ONS (constraint 3)

Excluded from every figure above, per instruction: capital conservation buffer, any countercyclical capital buffer amount, the supplementary leverage ratio (3% under § 3.10(a)(5)), and any supervisory add-on. Corroboration that this exclusion does not change the 2014 answer: § 3.300(a)(1) provides that 'From January 1, 2014 through December 31, 2015, a national bank or Federal savings association is not subject to limits on distributions and discretionary bonus payments under § 3.11 ... notwithstanding the amount of its capital conservation buffer or any applicable countercyclical capital buffer amount' — i.e., no buffer add-on operated in 2014 in any event. Also out of scope per the request: total capital ratio (8%) and leverage ratio (4%), both of which are quoted above only as part of the reproduced transition sentence, not as answers.

5. ASSUMPTIONS AND OPEN ITEMS FOR THE REVIEWER

- Entity: a national bank (or Federal branch) supervised by the OCC under 12 CFR Part 3, an advanced approaches institution, and NOT a savings and loan holding company. The SLHC variant has a different timing paragraph (§ 3.1(f)(2)(ii), beginning January 1, 2015) and is out of scope.
- 'Cited page' was not identified in the request. Both reproductions available for testing state the same § 3.10(a) figures: the 2014 CFR print (CFR-2014-title12-vol1, part 3, § 3.10) and the current eCFR (§ 3.10). The Ask 2 answer is therefore invariant across the two; if the reviewer's cited page is a different edition or amendment, re-verify against that edition's § 3.10(a).
- Version in force during 2014 governs Ask 1 (transition schedule as adopted at 78 FR 62157, 62273, Oct. 11, 2013, effective Jan. 1, 2014); the cited page's version governs Ask 2.
- Figures are regulatory minimums, not the bank's actual or reported ratios, and are not a capital adequacy conclusion for any specific institution.

6. VERIFICATION CHECKLIST (each figure traced to quoted text)

- 4.0% CET1 → 'maintain a minimum common equity tier 1 capital ratio of 4 percent' (eCFR § 3.1(f)(1)(iii)(A)). OK.
- 5.5% tier 1 → 'a minimum tier 1 capital ratio of 5.5 percent' (same). OK.
- 4.5% CET1 → 'A common equity tier 1 capital ratio of 4.5 percent' (2014 CFR print § 3.10(a)(1)); 'A common equity tier 1 capital ratio of 4.5 percent' (eCFR § 3.10(a)(1)(i)). OK.
- 6.0% tier 1 → 'A tier 1 capital ratio of 6 percent' (2014 CFR print § 3.10(a)(2)); 'A tier 1 capital ratio of 6 percent' (eCFR § 3.10(a)(1)(ii)). OK.
- Deltas 0.5 pp each computed as stated in section 1. OK.
- No buffer, SLR or other add-on included in any answer figure. OK.

=====================================================================
0. ANSWER UP FRONT
=====================================================================
Under the text of 12 CFR 329.21(b)(2) and (b)(3) as reproduced on the cited pages, and ignoring the other caps and adjustments (the 329.21(c)-(e) unadjusted excess HQLA deduction and the 329.21(f)-(i) adjusted amounts):

  Level 2A liquid asset amount = 0.85 x $80,000,000 = $68,000,000
  Level 2B liquid asset amount = 0.50 x $30,000,000 = $15,000,000
  Sum                          = $68,000,000 + $15,000,000 = $83,000,000

Period: the single 'calculation date' stipulated in the request (no specific calendar date given; all figures are as of that date).
Currency: US dollars (USD).
Basis: fair value of assets that are eligible HQLA as of the calculation date, per the request's stipulation; no haircuts or adjustments other than the statutory 85%/50% factors.
Units: stated in millions in the narrative ($80M, $30M), computed in whole dollars.

=====================================================================
1. SOURCE TEXT RELIED ON (quoted, not recalled)
=====================================================================
Primary source: 12 CFR 329.21, https://ecfr.gov/current/title-12/section-329.21 (fetched 2026-11-23T12:13:38Z, sha256 ca896132ac72).
Cross-checked against four further reproductions of Part 329, all identical in the operative language:
  - govinfo XML, 2026 edition, sha256 ce49f4018311
  - govinfo XHTML, 2026 edition, sha256 0ecf4fa9df6a
  - govinfo Subpart C XHTML, sha256 cc1e1f23af77
  - eCFR Part 329 landing page, sha256 f177572c4517
  (a 2025-edition govinfo copy, sha256 e5da7789e260, also matches)

Operative quotations:

[Q1] 329.21(b)(2): 'The level 2A liquid asset amount equals 85 percent of the fair value of all level 2A liquid assets held by the FDIC-supervised institution as of the calculation date that are eligible HQLA.'

[Q2] 329.21(b)(3): 'The level 2B liquid asset amount equals 50 percent of the fair value of all level 2B liquid assets held by the FDIC-supervised institution as of the calculation date that are eligible HQLA.'

[Q3] 329.21(a): HQLA amount = level 1 liquid asset amount + level 2A liquid asset amount + level 2B liquid asset amount - the greater of (i) the unadjusted excess HQLA amount and (ii) the adjusted excess HQLA amount.

[Q4] 329.21(c): unadjusted excess HQLA amount = level 2 cap excess amount + level 2B cap excess amount.

[Q5] 329.21(d): level 2 cap excess amount = greater of (1) (level 2A liquid asset amount + level 2B liquid asset amount - 0.6667 x level 1 liquid asset amount) and (2) 0.

[Q6] 329.21(e): level 2B cap excess amount = greater of (1) (level 2B liquid asset amount - level 2 cap excess amount - 0.1765 x (level 1 liquid asset amount + level 2A liquid asset amount)) and (2) 0.

[Q7] 329.21(f)-(i): adjusted level 1/2A/2B liquid asset amounts (30-day unwind basis) and the adjusted excess HQLA amount, computed with the same 0.6667 and 0.1765 factors applied to adjusted amounts.

=====================================================================
2. WHERE THE 'CAPS' ACTUALLY LIVE IN THIS TEXT (important correction)
=====================================================================
There is no '40%' and no '15%' anywhere in the reproduced text. The text contains:
  - 85% and 50%: these are the haircut factors that convert fair value into the level 2A and level 2B liquid asset amounts (329.21(b)(2), (b)(3)).
  - 0.6667 and 0.1765: these are the cap factors, applied against the LEVEL 1 liquid asset amount, inside the excess-HQLA deduction (329.21(d), (e)).

The familiar 40% / 15% figures are the implied caps, and they reconcile exactly to the text:
  - 0.6667 ~= 2/3. If level 2 (2A + 2B) <= (2/3) x level 1, then level 2 / total <= (2/3)/(1 + 2/3) = 0.4000 = 40%.
  - 0.1765 = 0.15/0.85 (0.15/0.85 = 0.176470588). If level 2B <= (0.15/0.85) x (level 1 + level 2A), then level 2B / total <= (0.15/0.85)/(1 + 0.15/0.85) = 0.15/1.00 = 15%.
Consequence for this request: the cap cannot be applied to the $80M/$30M fair values directly, because both cap tests are expressed relative to a level 1 liquid asset amount, and no level 1 amount is given. Applying 40% and 15% directly to $80M and $30M would be an arithmetic error that the text does not support.

=====================================================================
3. INPUTS (each labelled; assumptions marked)
=====================================================================
Input A  Fair value of level 2A liquid assets, eligible HQLA ... $80,000,000  [given in request; fair value basis; USD; as of calculation date]
Input B  Fair value of level 2B liquid assets, eligible HQLA ... $30,000,000  [given in request; fair value basis; USD; as of calculation date]
Factor C  85% level 2A factor ............................... 0.85        [SOURCE Q1, 329.21(b)(2)]
Factor D  50% level 2B factor ............................... 0.50        [SOURCE Q2, 329.21(b)(3)]
Input E   Level 1 liquid asset amount ....................... NOT PROVIDED  [required by 329.21(d),(e); see section 6]
Input F   Adjusted level 1/2A/2B amounts (30-day unwind) ..... NOT PROVIDED  [329.21(f)-(i); excluded per instruction]

ASSUMPTIONS (not facts):
  A-1  The $80M and $30M are fair values as of one single calculation date, in USD, with no currency translation and no date mismatch.
  A-2  All $80M and $30M are 'eligible HQLA' (329.22 operational requirements met), as stipulated by the request; no eligibility haircut is applied.
  A-3  'Ignoring other caps and adjustments' is read as: do not compute the 329.21(c)-(e) unadjusted excess HQLA deduction and do not compute the 329.21(f)-(i) adjusted amounts. Only 329.21(b)(2) and (b)(3) are applied.
  A-4  No reserve balance requirement or other level 1 item is in scope (none is given).
  A-5  This is a mechanical computation exercise, not a compliance determination, and not a representation about any actual institution.

=====================================================================
4. COMPUTATION (every step shown)
=====================================================================
Step 1 - Level 2A liquid asset amount (329.21(b)(2)):
   = 85% x Input A
   = 0.85 x $80,000,000
   = $68,000,000
   Check: 68,000,000 <= 80,000,000 (haircut direction correct); 80,000,000 - 68,000,000 = 12,000,000 implicit 15% haircut.

Step 2 - Level 2B liquid asset amount (329.21(b)(3)):
   = 50% x Input B
   = 0.50 x $30,000,000
   = $15,000,000
   Check: 15,000,000 <= 30,000,000; 30,000,000 - 15,000,000 = 15,000,000 implicit 50% haircut.

Step 3 - Sum of the two amounts (the quantity asked in ask 3):
   = $68,000,000 + $15,000,000
   = $83,000,000
   Check: 68 + 15 = 83; 83 <= 80 + 30 = 110 (total haircut of 27,000,000, i.e. 24.5455% blended on the 110,000,000 gross).

Step 4 - (Excluded by instruction) 329.21(d)/(e) excess HQLA deduction: cannot be computed, Input E missing. See section 6.

=====================================================================
5. RESULT TABLE
=====================================================================
Line | Item                                          | Amount (USD) | Basis / source
-----+-----------------------------------------------+--------------+---------------------------------------------
 1   | Fair value, level 2A eligible HQLA            |  80,000,000  | Given; fair value; calculation date
 2   | x 85% factor                                  |       0.85   | 329.21(b)(2), SOURCE Q1
 3   | = Level 2A liquid asset amount                |  68,000,000  | Line 1 x Line 2
 4   | Fair value, level 2B eligible HQLA            |  30,000,000  | Given; fair value; calculation date
 5   | x 50% factor                                  |       0.50   | 329.21(b)(3), SOURCE Q2
 6   | = Level 2B liquid asset amount                |  15,000,000  | Line 4 x Line 5
 7   | = SUM (Line 3 + Line 6)                       |  83,000,000  | 68,000,000 + 15,000,000

Note on line 7: $83,000,000 is the sum of the two level 2 liquid asset amounts only. It is NOT the HQLA amount under 329.21(a): the HQLA amount would also add the level 1 liquid asset amount and subtract the greater of the unadjusted and adjusted excess HQLA amounts, none of which is in scope or available here.

=====================================================================
6. WHAT WAS IGNORED, AND WHAT IT WOULD TAKE TO COMPUTE IT
=====================================================================
Excluded item 1 - Unadjusted excess HQLA amount (329.21(c)-(e)): requires the level 1 liquid asset amount (Input E), which is not given. Formula as written:
   L2 cap excess  = max(0, 2A_amt + 2B_amt - 0.6667 x L1)
   L2B cap excess = max(0, 2B_amt - L2 cap excess - 0.1765 x (L1 + 2A_amt))
Excluded item 2 - Adjusted excess HQLA amount (329.21(f)-(i)): requires the 30-day-unwind adjusted level 1/2A/2B amounts, which are not given.

Illustration ONLY (not part of the answer; shown so the reviewer can see the mechanics and challenge the base). Using the section 5 amounts:
  If L1 = $60,000,000:  L2 cap excess = max(0, 83,000,000 - 0.6667 x 60,000,000 = 40,002,000) = 42,998,000; L2B cap excess = max(0, 15,000,000 - 42,998,000 - 0.1765 x 128,000,000 = 22,592,000) = 0. HQLA = 60,000,000 + 83,000,000 - 42,998,000 = 100,002,000. Cross-check: allowed level 2 = (2/3) x 60,000,000 = 40,000,000; 60,000,000 + 40,000,000 = 100,000,000 (2,000 rounding from the 0.6667 factor).
  If L1 = $100,000,000: L2 cap excess = max(0, 83,000,000 - 66,670,000) = 16,330,000; L2B cap excess = max(0, 15,000,000 - 16,330,000 - 29,657,000) = 0. HQLA = 183,000,000 - 16,330,000 = 166,670,000. Cross-check: (2/3) x 100,000,000 = 66,667,000; 100,000,000 + 66,667,000 = 166,667,000.
  If L1 = $150,000,000: L2 cap excess = max(0, 83,000,000 - 100,005,000) = 0; L2B cap excess = max(0, 15,000,000 - 0 - 0.1765 x 218,000,000 = 38,477,000) = 0. HQLA = 233,000,000. Cross-check: level 2 share = 83/233 = 35.62% <= 40%; level 2B share = 15/233 = 6.44% <= 15%.
Observation from the illustration: the caps reduce the HQLA TOTAL via the excess deduction; they do not restate the 'level 2A liquid asset amount' or 'level 2B liquid asset amount' line items, which remain 85%/50% of fair value by definition in (b)(2)/(b)(3).

=====================================================================
7. REVIEW POINTS / LIMITATIONS
=====================================================================
1. The request's framing ('level 2A cap' / 'level 2B cap') does not match the text: the caps are 0.6667 and 0.1765 factors against level 1 inside the excess-HQLA deduction. If the reviewer intends the post-cap HQLA contribution rather than the (b)(2)/(b)(3) amounts, a level 1 liquid asset amount must be supplied; until then that variant cannot be computed. The section 6 illustration is provided for that purpose only.
2. Calculation date, currency confirmation, and fair-value measurement date/level (ASC 820 hierarchy) are not specified in the request; all figures here are as stipulated.
3. Eligibility as HQLA (329.22 operational requirements, e.g. unencumbered, under control of the institution, 329.22(b) asset-specific conditions) is stipulated, not tested.
4. Rounding: exact at the stated amounts; no rounding applied. The 0.6667 and 0.1765 factors are the regulation's own rounded constants (2/3 = 0.666667; 0.15/0.85 = 0.176471), so any downstream use introduces up to a few thousand dollars of rounding on $100M-scale balances.
5. Cross-source verification: the five fetched reproductions of Part 329 agree word-for-word on 329.21(b)(2), (b)(3), (c), (d), (e), (h) and (i), so the arithmetic above is not sensitive to which cited page is treated as authoritative.

MEMORANDUM - Minimum CET1 and Tier 1 capital ratios, calendar year 2014
Entity: advanced approaches national bank, not a savings and loan holding company (predicate supplied by requester; taken as given, not independently verified).
Period: January 1, 2014 through December 31, 2014, inclusive.
Currency: underlying capital and RWA amounts in USD; the answers are ratios and therefore currency-neutral.
Basis: regulatory capital divided by total risk-weighted assets as defined in 12 CFR Part 3. For an advanced approaches bank that has completed the parallel run, the CET1 and tier 1 ratios are the LOWER of the standardized and advanced approaches calculations (12 CFR 3.10(c) in the 2014 edition; redesignated 3.10(d) in later editions). The minimum requirement percentages below are the same on either calculation.

1. ASK 1 - MINIMUM RATIOS APPLYING JANUARY 1 - DECEMBER 31, 2014
Source: 12 CFR 3.10(f)(1)(iii)(A), 'Timing': 'From January 1, 2014 to December 31, 2014, maintain a minimum common equity tier 1 capital ratio of 4 percent, a minimum tier 1 capital ratio of 5.5 percent, a minimum total capital ratio of 8 percent, and a minimum leverage ratio of 4 percent.' (Text as reproduced in the current eCFR at ecfr.gov/current/title-12/chapter-I/part-3, in the 2024 CFR at govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2024-title12-vol1/xml/CFR-2024-title12-vol1-part3.xml, and in the 2026 CFR.)

  Ratio                     | Minimum, 1/1/2014-12/31/2014 | Source
  Common equity tier 1      | 4.0%                          | 12 CFR 3.10(f)(1)(iii)(A)
  Tier 1                    | 5.5%                          | 12 CFR 3.10(f)(1)(iii)(A)
  (context) Total capital   | 8.0%                          | 12 CFR 3.10(f)(1)(iii)(A)
  (context) Leverage        | 4.0%                          | 12 CFR 3.10(f)(1)(iii)(A)

These are the transition-year floors. They are the operative requirement for 2014 and they displace the fully phased-in figures in 3.10(a) for that year, because 3.10(f)(1) is expressly '[s]ubject to the transition provisions in subpart G of this part' and fixes the 2014 schedule in subparagraph (iii)(A).

2. ASK 2 - MINIMUM RATIOS IN THE TEXT OF 12 CFR PART 3 REPRODUCED ON THE CITED PAGE
Source: 12 CFR 3.10(a)(1)(i)-(ii): '(i) A common equity tier 1 capital ratio of 4.5 percent. (ii) A tier 1 capital ratio of 6 percent.'

  Ratio                | Minimum stated in 3.10(a)(1) | Source
  Common equity tier 1 | 4.5%                         | 12 CFR 3.10(a)(1)(i)

Every reproduction fetched for this engagement states 3.10(a) identically, so the answer is robust to which page is meant: (a) govinfo CFR-2014-title12-vol1-part3.pdf (the edition in force during 2014); (b) govinfo CFR-2024-title12-vol1-part3.xml; (c) ecfr.gov/current/title-12/chapter-I/part-3; (d) ecfr.gov/current/title-12/part-3/section-3.10; and (e) govinfo CFR-2026-title12-vol1-part3.html.

  CET1: 4.5% - 4.0% = 0.5 percentage points = 50 basis points.
  Tier 1: 6.0% - 5.5% = 0.5 percentage points = 50 basis points.
This is not a discrepancy between sources; it is the transition mechanics inside the same section. 3.10(a) states the fully phased-in minimums; 3.10(f)(1)(iii)(A) states the lower floors that apply during 2014. verdict.summary:
DRAFT FOR REVIEW BY A QUALIFIED FINANCE/REGULATORY-REPORTING PROFESSIONAL. Not financial, tax, investment or regulatory advice.

=== 1. SCOPE, PERIOD, CURRENCY, BASIS ===
- Entity: an FDIC-supervised institution subject to 12 CFR Part 329 (Liquidity Risk Measurement Standards).
- Period: a single calculation date (the date is not specified in the request; all figures are 'as of the calculation date').
- Currency: USD (assumed from the '$' notation and the FDIC/Part 329 context; not independently confirmed).
- Basis: fair value of assets that are eligible HQLA. The request states all $80 million of level 2A and all $30 million of level 2B assets are eligible HQLA, so no eligibility haircut/attribution is applied.
- Inputs (given, not derived): level 2A fair value = $80,000,000; level 2B fair value = $30,000,000.

=== 2. GOVERNING TEXT (source of the factors) ===
Reproduced 12 CFR 329.21(b), as fetched from the cited pages (eCFR §329.21, eCFR Part 329, eCFR Subpart C, and GovInfo CFR 2026 title 12 vol. 5 — all four reproductions are word-for-word identical on these two paragraphs):

  '(2) Level 2A liquid asset amount. The level 2A liquid asset amount equals 85 percent of the fair value of all level 2A liquid assets held by the FDIC-supervised institution as of the calculation date that are eligible HQLA.'

  '(3) Level 2B liquid asset amount. The level 2B liquid asset amount equals 50 percent of the fair value of all level 2B liquid assets held by the FDIC-supervised institution as of the calculation date that are eligible HQLA.'

Sources: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-12/section-329.21 (sha256 ca896132ac72); https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-12/part-329 (sha256 f177572c4517); https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-12/chapter-III/subchapter-B/part-329/subpart-C (sha256 027bbd837910); https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2026-title12-vol5/xml/CFR-2026-title12-vol5-part329.xml (sha256 ce49f4018311).

Note on the project-context assumption: the assumption that level 2B might be haircut at 25%–50% by asset subclass is NOT supported by the reproduced text. Section 329.21(b)(3) applies a single 50 percent factor to the level 2B liquid asset amount; the asset-type distinctions in §329.20(c) (corporate debt, Russell 1000 common equity, municipal obligations) define what qualifies as level 2B, they do not set different haircut factors in §329.21. The 50 percent factor is used here.

=== 3. HAIRCUT DERIVATION ===
The regulation is written as a retention percentage, not a haircut; the haircut is the complement.
- Level 2A: retention 85% → haircut = 100% − 85% = 15%.
- Level 2B: retention 50% → haircut = 100% − 50% = 50%.

=== 4. CALCULATION (all arithmetic shown) ===
Level 2A liquid asset amount
  = 85% × fair value of eligible level 2A assets
  = 0.85 × $80,000,000
  = $68,000,000
  (equivalently: $80,000,000 − 15% × $80,000,000 = $80,000,000 − $12,000,000 = $68,000,000)

Level 2B liquid asset amount
  = 50% × fair value of eligible level 2B assets
  = 0.50 × $30,000,000
  = $15,000,000
  (equivalently: $30,000,000 − 50% × $30,000,000 = $30,000,000 − $15,000,000 = $15,000,000)

Sum of the two liquid asset amounts
  = $68,000,000 + $15,000,000
  = $83,000,000

Total haircut taken: $110,000,000 − $83,000,000 = $27,000,000 (= $12,000,000 + $15,000,000).

=== 5. WHAT IS EXCLUDED BY 'IGNORING OTHER CAPS AND ADJUSTMENTS' ===
The $68,000,000 / $15,000,000 / $83,000,000 figures are the §329.21(b)(2) and (b)(3) liquid asset amounts only. They are PRE-CAP and PRE-ADJUSTMENT. Explicitly not applied, and each would require data the request does not supply:
(a) Level 2 cap excess amount, §329.21(d): greater of [level 2A + level 2B − 0.6667 × level 1 liquid asset amount] and 0. Requires the level 1 liquid asset amount, which is not given.
(b) Level 2B cap excess amount, §329.21(e): greater of [level 2B − level 2 cap excess − 0.1765 × (level 1 + level 2A)] and 0. Requires level 1.
(c) Unadjusted excess HQLA amount, §329.21(c) = (a) + (b); and the §329.21(a)(4) subtraction of the greater of the unadjusted and adjusted excess HQLA amounts.
(d) Adjusted liquid asset amounts, §329.21(f), and adjusted excess HQLA amount, §329.21(g)–(i) — these require the unwind of secured funding/lending, asset exchanges and collateralized derivatives transactions maturing within 30 calendar days of the calculation date.
(e) The reserve balance requirement deduction from level 1 under §329.21(b)(1) and Regulation D §204.5 (no level 1 assets are in scope).
(f) Operational requirements for eligible HQLA under §329.22 — taken as satisfied because the request stipulates the assets are eligible HQLA.

Material caveat for the reviewer: because the level 2 / level 2B caps in §329.21(d)–(e) are driven by 0.6667 × level 1 and 0.1765 × (level 1 + level 2A), the $83,000,000 sum is NOT an HQLA amount under §329.21(a). If level 1 were zero, the level 2 cap excess amount would equal the entire $83,000,000 and the HQLA contribution of these assets would be reduced to zero. The $83,000,000 is only the sum of the two post-haircut liquid asset amounts before any cap.

=== 6. RESULT ===
Level 2A liquid asset amount: $68,000,000 (USD, as of the calculation date, 85% of $80,000,000 fair value).
Level 2B liquid asset amount: $15,000,000 (USD, as of the calculation date, 50% of $30,000,000 fair value).
Sum: $83,000,000 (USD, pre-cap, pre-adjustment).

=== 7. ASSUMPTIONS AND LIMITATIONS (flag for reviewer) ===
1. The reproduced text is treated as the current, operative version of 12 CFR 329.21; the four fetched reproductions agree, but currency of the cited page against the current eCFR should be confirmed as of the actual calculation date.
2. All $80,000,000 of level 2A and all $30,000,000 of level 2B assets are eligible HQLA and meet §329.22 operational requirements (stipulated by the request).
3. No level 1 liquid assets, no reserve balance requirement, and no 30-day unwind transactions are in scope.
4. Currency is USD and amounts are stated in nominal dollars with no present-value discounting.
5. Figures are rounded to the dollar as given ($ millions); no rounding difference arises at the stated precision.

verdict.summary:
# Minimum CET1 and Tier 1 Ratios — Advanced Approaches National Bank, Calendar Year 2014

Draft for review by a qualified finance or accounting professional. Not financial, tax, investment or legal advice. All ratios are regulatory minimums **excluding** the capital conservation buffer, any countercyclical capital buffer amount, any G-SIB surcharge and any other add-on (per the request's constraint 3).

**Scope / basis statement (applies to every figure below):**
- **Entity:** an OCC-regulated national bank that is an *advanced approaches* institution and is **not** a savings and loan holding company. Governing rule: **12 CFR Part 3** (OCC), not the Federal Reserve's Regulation Q (12 CFR Part 217) and not the FRB's holding-company rule.
- **Period:** January 1, 2014 through December 31, 2014 (single calendar year; the transition year, not a phase-in average).
- **Currency:** none — the deliverable is expressed in **percent** (dimensionless ratios). Capital amounts are in **USD** wherever a dollar illustration appears, and that illustration is labelled as hypothetical.
- **Basis of each ratio:** regulatory capital numerator (common equity tier 1 capital, or tier 1 capital) over the denominator prescribed by Part 3 for the period. For this entity during 2014 the denominator is **advanced approaches total risk-weighted assets** — see § 3.10(f)(1)(i): advanced approaches RWA is calculated beginning January 1, 2014, and standardized total risk-weighted assets are not calculated until beginning January 1, 2015. This affects the *denominator*, not the percentage minimums in the answers.

---

## 1. Answer table

| # | Question | CET1 minimum | Tier 1 minimum | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Minimum ratios that **applied** 1 Jan – 31 Dec 2014 (transitional) | **4.0%** | **5.5%** | 12 CFR 3.10(f)(1)(iii)(A) — the 2014 timing/transition provision |
| 2 | Corresponding minimums stated in the **text of Part 3** (steady state) | **4.5%** | **6.0%** | 12 CFR 3.10(a)(1)(i) and (a)(1)(ii) |

For completeness (not asked, but in the same sentence of the rule and useful for a checklist): the 2014 transitional **total capital** ratio was **8%** and the **leverage** ratio was **4%**, and the steady-state minimums in § 3.10(a)(1)(iii)–(iv) are also **8%** and **4%** — i.e. total capital and leverage did not phase in.

---

## 2. Source extracts (verbatim, with citation)

**Source A — current codified text, 12 CFR 3.10(f)(1)(iii) ("Timing"), as reproduced on the cited eCFR page** (https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-12/chapter-I/part-3, fetched 2026-11-23):

> "(f) Timing. (1) Subject to the transition provisions in subpart G of this part, an advanced approaches national bank or Federal savings association that is not a savings and loan holding company must: … (iii) Beginning on January 1, 2014, calculate and maintain minimum capital ratios in accordance with subparts A, B, and C of this part, provided, however, that such national bank or Federal savings association must: (A) **From January 1, 2014 to December 31, 2014, maintain a minimum common equity tier 1 capital ratio of 4 percent, a minimum tier 1 capital ratio of 5.5 percent**, a minimum total capital ratio of 8 percent, and a minimum leverage ratio of 4 percent; and (B) From January 1, 2015 to December 31, 2017, an advanced approaches national bank …"

**Source B — current codified text, 12 CFR 3.10(a)(1) ("Minimum capital requirements"), same cited eCFR page:**

> "(a) Minimum capital requirements. (1) A national bank or Federal savings association must maintain the following minimum capital ratios: (i) A **common equity tier 1 capital ratio of 4.5 percent**. (ii) A **tier 1 capital ratio of 6 percent**. (iii) A total capital ratio of 8 percent. (iv) A leverage ratio of 4 percent. (v) For advanced approaches national banks … a supplementary leverage ratio of 3 percent. …"

**Source C — corroboration in the 2014 print of the CFR** (CFR-2014-title12-vol1, Part 3, § 3.10, https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2014-title12-vol1/pdf/CFR-2014-title12-vol1-part3.pdf, fetched 2026-11-23). The print reproduces both the same steady-state list ("(2) A tier 1 capital ratio of 6 percent. (3) A total capital ratio of 8 percent. (4) A leverage ratio of 4 percent. …") and the same 2014 transition sentence: "… **5.5 percent**, a minimum total capital ratio of 8 percent, and a minimum leverage ratio of 4 percent; and (B) From January 1, 2015 to December 31, 2017, an advanced approaches national bank …".

**Source D — 12 CFR 3.300 (subpart G, Transitions),** https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-12/part-3/subpart-G : "(a) Capital conservation and countercyclical capital buffer. (1) From January 1, 2014 through December 31, 2015, a national bank … is not subject to limits on distributions and discretionary bonus payments under § 3.11 … notwithstanding the amount of its capital conservation buffer or any applicable countercyclical capital buffer amount." → Confirms that **no buffer requirement bites in 2014**, consistent with the instruction to ignore buffers and add-ons. This is why the answer set is exactly {4.0%, 5.5%} and not {4.0% + 0.625% or +2.5%, …}.

Rule source line for Part 3 subpart B: **78 FR 62157, 62273 (Oct. 11, 2013)** — the Basel III regulatory capital rule that established this transition schedule.

---

## 3. Reconciliation of the two answers (arithmetic shown)

| Ratio | 2014 transitional (applied) | Part 3 text steady state | Difference |
|---|---|---|---|
| Common equity tier 1 | 4.0% | 4.5% | 4.5 − 4.0 = **0.5 pp lower in 2014** |
| Tier 1 | 5.5% | 6.0% | 6.0 − 5.5 = **0.5 pp lower in 2014** |
| Total capital | 8.0% | 8.0% | 0.0 pp |
| Leverage | 4.0% | 4.0% | 0.0 pp |

The mechanism: § 3.10(f)(1) opens with "**Subject to the transition provisions in subpart G of this part**" and then states that the bank "must calculate and maintain minimum capital ratios in accordance with subparts A, B, and C **provided, however, that** …" the 2014 figures apply. The "provided, however" clause is the operative override: for 1 Jan – 31 Dec 2014 the binding minimums are 4.0% / 5.5%, and the 4.5% / 6.0% figures in § 3.10(a)(1) are the **steady-state** minimums that become binding from **January 1, 2015** (the phase-in step in paragraph (f)(1)(iii)(B) and the 2015 column of the transition schedule). Both sets of numbers are correct; they answer different questions (applicable-in-2014 vs. as-written-in-the-rule-text).

**Illustrative dollar translation (hypothetical, for reviewer convenience only).** Assume advanced approaches total risk-weighted assets of **$100.0 billion** at every quarter-end in 2014 (assumption, not a fact about any bank):
- 2014 minimum CET1 = 4.0% × $100.0bn = **$4.00bn**; steady-state would be 4.5% × $100.0bn = $4.50bn → $0.50bn lower requirement in 2014.
- 2014 minimum tier 1 = 5.5% × $100.0bn = **$5.50bn**; steady-state would be 6.0% × $100.0bn = $6.00bn → $0.50bn lower requirement in 2014.
- Arithmetic: 0.040 × 100.0 = 4.00; 0.045 × 100.0 = 4.50; 4.50 − 4.00 = 0.50. 0.055 × 100.0 = 5.50; 0.060 × 100.0 = 6.00; 6.00 − 5.50 = 0.50.

---

## 4. Applicability checks (why the OCC Part 3 numbers, and no other set, apply)

1. **Charter/regulator:** national bank → OCC → 12 CFR Part 3. Not the FRB's 12 CFR Part 217 (holding company) and not the FDIC's Part 324.
2. **Not an SLHC:** the request states the bank is not a savings and loan holding company. § 3.10(f)(1) is expressly addressed to "an advanced approaches national bank … **that is not a savings and loan holding company**", so this entity falls squarely in § 3.10(f)(1)(iii)(A) rather than any SLHC-specific timing paragraph.
3. **Advanced approaches status:** it changes the *timing* (advanced approaches RWA calculated from 1/1/2014) and the *denominator* (see below), and it triggers the 3% supplementary leverage ratio in § 3.10(a)(1)(v) — but it does **not** change the 4.0% / 5.5% minimums for 2014. No advanced-approaches-specific higher CET1 or tier 1 minimum existed for 2014.
4. **Denominator nuance to flag for the reviewer:** under § 3.10(c), an advanced approaches bank that has completed the parallel run process and received OCC notification under § 3.121(d) reports each ratio as the **lower** of the standardized-RWA ratio and the advanced-approaches-RWA ratio. During 2014, standardized total risk-weighted assets are not yet required to be calculated (§ 3.10(f)(1)(i): standardized RWA begins 1/1/2015), so in practice the 2014 ratio is measured against **advanced approaches total risk-weighted assets**. The percentage minimums are unaffected.

---

## 5. Checklist reconciliation and discrepancy handling

- If the legacy checklist carries **4.0% CET1 / 5.5% tier 1** for calendar 2014, it **agrees** with § 3.10(f)(1)(iii)(A) and can be signed off on that point (subject to the denominator and buffer-exclusion notes above).
- If the legacy checklist instead carries **4.5% / 6.0%** for calendar 2014, it is applying the **steady-state** minimums one year early. That is a mis-mapping of the transition schedule, not a different reading of the rule; the correction is to move 4.5% / 6.0% to the 2015-and-later column.
- If the legacy checklist carries a **buffered** figure (e.g. 5.5% CET1 or 7.0% tier 1, i.e. 4.5% + 2.5% or 4.5% + 2.5% / 6.0% + 2.5% in later years), it is measuring a different thing; per the instruction, buffers and add-ons are excluded here, and § 3.300(a)(1) confirms no buffer-based distribution limits applied in 2014 in any event.
- **Vintage caveat:** the current eCFR text has been amended since 2013 (e.g. Category III references in § 3.10(a)(1)(v), the community bank leverage ratio paragraph (a)(2), CECL transition language in subpart G). None of those amendments alter § 3.10(a)(1)(i)–(ii) or the 2014 transition sentence in § 3.10(f)(1)(iii)(A), and the 2014 CFR print independently confirms both, so the answer is stable across the two vintages.

---

## 6. Assumptions (each is an assumption, not a rule fact)

| # | Assumption | Effect if wrong |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | The entity is an OCC-supervised national bank subject to Part 3 (not a state member bank, state nonmember bank, or federal savings association) | A different regulator's substantively parallel rule would apply; the 2014 numbers would be the same in substance but the citation would change |
| A2 | The "cited page" is the eCFR Part 3 page and/or the 2014 CFR print of Part 3, both of which reproduce the same two sets of figures | If a different vintage were cited, re-verify § 3.10(a)(1)(i)–(ii) and § 3.10(f)(1)(iii)(A) against that text |
| A3 | Buffers, countercyclical buffer amounts, G-SIB surcharges and any other add-ons are excluded from both columns | Including them would raise the applicable figures; they are excluded by instruction |
| A4 | The $100.0bn RWA figure in §3 is hypothetical | Only the illustrative dollar amounts change; no percentage changes |

**Reviewer sign-off points:** (i) confirm the checklist's 2014 column reads 4.0% / 5.5%; (ii) confirm the denominator used in the 2014 ratio calculations is advanced approaches total risk-weighted assets; (iii) confirm the comparison column against the rule text is labelled "steady state / from 1 January 2015" so the two answer sets are not conflated.
